newsitem.title: USA: Albright confirms around the world trip.
newsitem.headline: Albright confirms around the world trip.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday confirmed plans to make an around the globe trip to selected world capitals in February.
Albright did not disclose dates or specific capitals to be visited. But she told her first news conference:

"I plan during the next several weeks to meet with my counterparts from a number of capitals. We haven't worked out the details, but I expect to make a trip sometime in February to parts of Europe and Asia."
Earlier, officials had said the dates would be February 12-22, but on Friday they said those may be shifting somewhat as the State Department seeks to work out her itinerary.

Albright said the purpose of her first overseas travel "will be to establish good personal and working relationships, and to renew acquaintances with leaders I have met, and to get to know those that I have not met yet."

"The destinations, obviously, are not accidental. As I told the Senate committee, we believe that America's key alliances and relationships are the bonds that hold together not only our foreign policy, but also the entire international system," she said.
Albright did not seem eager to schedule a trip to the Middle East, the region to which her predecessor, Warren Christopher, travelled the most.

She assured that she is committed, like President Bill Clinton, to achieving a comprehensive peace in the region and believes it is important for the secretary of state to be involved in that process.
But as for a visit there, she said she would be guided by the advice of Dennis Ross, the special U.S. Mideast coordinator.
Christopher was the most-travelled U.S. secretary of state, logging more than 700,000 miles in four years in office. Albright said, however, "I don't view this as a challenge."
